chunks.label: Quick gut reactions
chunks.rationale: Lets you react out loud to food, drinks and gross things.
chunks.interference: Mazui usually means 'this is bad', not just bad taste.

chunks.label: Why and somehow
chunks.rationale: Lets you ask why and admit you don't know why.
chunks.interference: Nandaka, nazeka and nantonaku all mean 'somehow' and blur together.

chunks.label: Definitely, no matter what
chunks.rationale: Lets you promise, insist and invite with conviction.
chunks.interference: Zehi is for wishes and invitations, kanarazu for promises and facts.

chunks.label: Suddenly and all at once
chunks.rationale: Lets you describe abrupt changes and ones you didn't notice.
chunks.interference: Totsuzen and ikinari overlap; ikinari is more casual and often a complaint.

chunks.label: How you do or say it
chunks.rationale: Lets you say something is done properly, clearly or directly.
chunks.interference: Shikkari and kichinto both mean properly; shikkari adds effort, kichinto neatness.

chunks.label: On purpose or forced
chunks.rationale: Lets you say whether something was intended, forced or a kind effort.
chunks.interference: Wazawaza (kindly went out of your way) and wazato (did it on purpose) are easy to swap.

chunks.label: By chance
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about luck, coincidence and unlikely possibilities.

chunks.label: Finally and coming soon
chunks.rationale: Lets you mark a long-awaited moment that has arrived or is about to.
chunks.interference: Iyoiyo looks ahead to what's about to happen; tsui ni and toutou look back.

chunks.label: Right away, on the spot
chunks.rationale: Lets you say something happens immediately or at the same moment.
chunks.interference: Sassato is an impatient 'hurry up', sassoku an eager 'right away'.

chunks.label: Still, already, originally
chunks.rationale: Lets you compare now with how things were before.
chunks.interference: Imada ni (still) and tokku ni (long ago) point in opposite directions.

chunks.label: Sooner or later
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about a vague future and how long things last.
chunks.interference: Sono uchi 'sometime soon' and ima no uchi 'while you still can' sound alike.

chunks.label: Again, for now, never again
chunks.rationale: Lets you say when something pauses, carries on or happens again.
chunks.interference: Nido to needs a negative verb, unlike mata 'again'.

chunks.label: Grumbles and hassles
chunks.rationale: Lets you complain about fussing, bad timing and hassle.
chunks.interference: Fuben is for things and places, not for a time that doesn't suit you.

chunks.label: Small requests and advice
chunks.rationale: Lets you add favours, precautions and gentle advice to what you ask.
chunks.interference: Nen no tame (just in case) gets mixed with mangaichi (if by some chance).

chunks.label: Of course, actually, apparently
chunks.rationale: Lets you frame a fact as obvious, real, inferred or unfortunate.
chunks.interference: Douyara is a guess from evidence; jissai states what is really so.

chunks.label: As expected or not
chunks.rationale: Lets you compare things with what you'd expect.
chunks.interference: Masa ni (exactly) sounds like masaka (no way!), and sasuga ni differs from sasuga (well done!).

drops.reason: Duplicate of 一気に; the bare noun is a tokenizer fragment of ikki ni.
